title: Same and different: comparing two things
keyIdea: To compare two things, look at one part at a time: the shape, the colour, the size, how many, what it can do. A quick look at the whole thing misses a lot. For each part, say if it is the same or different. Use both for what is the same: 'Both have four legs.' Use but for what is different: 'The cat is small, but the horse is big.' Two things can be the same in one way and different in another. A strawberry and a fire engine are both red, but one is tiny and one is huge. So 'the same' always means 'the same what?'. Some things only one of them has, some things both have, and some differences are so small that you only find them by checking every part.
familyTip: Put a spoon and a fork side by side, or two shoes, or two leaves from the park. Take turns: one of you says a way they are the same with 'both', the other says a way they are different with 'but'. Keep going until you run out. Then try two pictures in a book that nearly match.

visual.caption: An apple and a ball. Is each part the same or different? Drag each card into a box, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: compare a cat and a horse part by part, fill gaps with both or but, sort duck and fish cards, and spot a tiny difference.

kid: Look at a cat and a horse. Are they the same? Do not just look fast. Check one thing at a time. Legs: both have four legs. Same! Size: the cat is small, but the horse is big. Different!
Two little words help. Both tells what is the same: both are furry. But tells what is different: a cat says miaow, but a horse says neigh.
Some things only one has. A duck has feathers. A fish has fins. Some things both have: both can swim. So we can sort it three ways: only the duck, both, or only the fish.

Things can be the same in one way and different in another. A strawberry and a fire engine are both red, but one is tiny. Some differences are tiny too, like a missing door handle. Check every part, big and small.
adult: Ages 4 to 5. Development Matters (2021) lists 'making links and noticing patterns' as a part of creating and thinking critically. In Reception, children 'compare and contrast' characters from stories. The EYFS Early Learning Goals ask them to know 'similarities and differences' between places, times and communities. Key words: same, different, both, but, compare.

Comparing is a way to learn, not only a quiz game. Gentner (2010) shows that putting two things side by side helps young children notice what they share. So the lab always shows the pair side by side and asks about one feature at a time.

Common mistakes: calling two things simply different after a quick glance; thinking same means the same in every way; mixing up both and but; putting a shared feature, such as swimming, on one side only; and stopping once the big differences are found, so a small one is missed.

In the lab, children check a cat and a horse feature by feature. They drag both or but into a sentence gap. They sort six duck and fish cards into three boxes. They find the one way two unlike things match. Last, they check two houses part by part for a tiny difference.

practice.prompt: Same and different: comparing two things. A cat and a horse both have four legs. Is that the same or different?
practice.hint: Count the legs on each one. Do the numbers match?
practice.explain: The cat has 4 legs and the horse has 4 legs, so that part is the same. Their size is different.

practice.prompt: Sam finds {n} ways a cup and a mug are the same and 2 ways they are different. How many ways did he find in all?
practice.hint: Put the same ways and the different ways together, then count them all.
practice.explain: {n} same and 2 different make {=n+2} ways. Checking one part at a time finds lots of them.

practice.prompt: Two pictures have {n} differences. Mia has found {k} of them. How many more must she find?
practice.hint: Take the ones she found away from all the differences.
practice.explain: {n} take away {k} leaves {=n-k}. She should check each part, even the small ones.

practice.prompt: Which word tells us what is the same?
practice.hint: Say it about a cat and a horse: ____ have four legs.
practice.explain: Both tells what is the same: both have four legs. But tells what is different.

practice.prompt: A duck and a fish can both swim. Where does 'can swim' go?
practice.hint: Can a duck swim? Can a fish swim?
practice.explain: Ducks and fish can both swim, so 'can swim' goes in the middle box: both.

pool.prompt: A strawberry and a fire engine. How are they the same?
pool.hint: Look at the colour of each one.
pool.explain: Both are red. But a strawberry is tiny and a fire engine is huge, so they are only the same in one way.

pool.prompt: The cat is small, ____ the horse is big. Which word fits the gap?
pool.hint: Small and big are different. Which word tells a difference?
pool.explain: But tells what is different: the cat is small, but the horse is big.

pool.prompt: Zoe looks at a spoon and a fork for one second and says 'They are just different.' What should she do?
choices: Check one part at a time
pool.hint: A quick look misses things. How can she look more carefully?
pool.explain: Checking one part at a time shows they are both metal and both have a handle, but only the fork has prongs.

pool.prompt: A duck and a fish. Where does 'has feathers' go?
pool.explain: Only the duck has feathers. A fish has scales instead.

pool.prompt: A ball and an orange are both round. Are they the same in every way?
choices: No, you can only eat the orange
Yes, round means all the same
No, they are not the same in any way
pool.hint: Same shape. What about eating them?
pool.explain: They are the same shape, but you can eat an orange and not a ball. Same in one way, different in another.

pool.prompt: Ben checks {n} parts of two teddies. Only 1 part is different. How many parts are the same?
pool.hint: Take the 1 different part away from all the parts he checked.
pool.explain: {n} parts take away 1 different part leaves {=n-1} parts that are the same.

pool.prompt: Lily sorts {a} cards into Only the duck and {b} cards into Both. How many cards did she sort?
pool.hint: Put the two groups of cards together and count them.
pool.explain: {a} and {b} make {=a+b} cards. The Both cards are things the duck and the fish share.

pool.prompt: Two houses nearly match. One door has no handle. What kind of difference is that?
choices: A tiny one you find by checking each part
A big one you see at once
pool.hint: Is a door handle big or small?
pool.explain: A missing handle is a tiny difference. You find it by checking each part of both houses.

pool.prompt: A penguin and a robin. Which is the same for both?
pool.hint: Penguins swim instead of flying. What do both of them have?
pool.explain: Both have wings, but only the robin can fly. A penguin uses its wings to swim.
